## TASK-DOC-001 — Plan (review only)

### Objective, IDs, completion
- **Objective:** Convert authoritative MySQL ticket state into stable labeled text.
- **IDs:** RAG-002, RAG-010, AC-010.
- **Depends on:** TASK-RIF-004, TASK-SVC-003.
- **Complete when:** Output is **deterministic** and contains **no Bootcamp resource/FAQ** data.
- **Verify:** Golden unit tests — assigned/unassigned, comments, resolution absent/present, **all statuses**.

### Searchable knowledge text (ticket fields only)
Per RAG-002 + `rag-ingestion.md` §2: **ticket ID, title, description, status, priority, assignee display (or `UNASSIGNED`), category, ordered comment bodies, resolution information when present.**  
Not in DOC-001 text: Bootcamp resources/FAQs, indexing-state, embeddings, unrelated entities.

### Proposed deterministic format (+ example)
Stable labeled sections, fixed order 1–9 (`rag-ingestion.md` §2):

```
Ticket ID: 42
Title: Cannot reset password
Description: Reset link returns 500.
Status: OPEN
Priority: HIGH
Assignee: Jane Doe
Category: account-access
Comments:
- First comment body
- Second comment body
Resolution Information: Cleared cache; link works.
```
(Omit the Resolution section entirely when absent. Use `Assignee: UNASSIGNED` when null.)

### Description / comments / resolution
| Section | Rule |
|---|---|
| Description | Always present (required domain field). |
| Comments | After Category; order by **creation timestamp, then ID**; empty list → empty Comments section (still labeled). Spec does **not** require author/timestamp in text—only ordered comment content. |
| Resolution | **Last**; include **only when present** (non-null/non-blank). |

### Title / status / priority / assignee / category — text vs metadata
| Field | Text (DOC-001) | Metadata (DOC-002) |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Yes | No (not in required chunk metadata list) |
| Status, priority, category | Yes | Yes |
| Assignee | Display / `UNASSIGNED` in text | `assigneeId` (nullable) + `assigneeDisplay` |
| Ticket ID | Yes | `ticketId` (+ `ticketVersion`, `chunkIndex` later) |

RAG-010 / §3: metadata ≥ ticket ID, status, priority, assignee, category. Title lives in **text**; status/priority/assignee/category in **both**.

### Null / blank
- Omit null optional content **except assignee** → always explicit `UNASSIGNED` (`rag-ingestion.md` §2).
- Resolution: omit section if null/blank.
- Required fields (title, description, status, priority, category) are nonblank in domain; builder should not invent values.

### Deterministic ordering
1. Fixed section order: ID → Title → Description → Status → Priority → Assignee → Category → Comments → Resolution (if any).  
2. Comments: creation timestamp, then ID.  
3. Same MySQL state → identical document string (no FAQ/resource noise).

### Ownership split
| Task | Owns |
|---|---|
| **DOC-001** | Builder + **immutable intermediate document** (labeled text only). |
| **DOC-002** | Provenance/grounding **metadata** on chunk inputs (`ticketId`, `ticketVersion`, `chunkIndex`, status, priority, assigneeId, assigneeDisplay, category). |
| **EMB-001** | Chunking (1600/200, boundaries)—**not** this task. |

DOC-001: no chunking, embedding, or PGVector writes.

### Minimum Java surface
- Knowledge-document **builder**
- **Immutable** intermediate document model
- Golden **unit tests** (cases above)

### Domain mismatch
**Aligned** with `SupportTicket` / `SupportTicketComment` / existing VOs (`title`, `description`, `priority`, `status`, `category`, `resolutionInformation`, optional `assignee` → `UNASSIGNED` / `User.fullName`, comment `body`, order by created+ID).  
**No invented fields.** Soft-delete/audit/indexing state are out of DOC-001 text. Comment **author** not required in canonical section text by `rag-ingestion.md` §2.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Tests are now enabled via JUnit Platform.

Designing the immutable `TicketKnowledgeDocument` record for the deterministic builder. The model will store canonical labeled text and preserve stable section ordering.

Evaluating whether the immutable model should expose raw structured fields or only the rendered text. The richer model would preserve individual sections for later processing.

Settled on a minimal immutable `TicketKnowledgeDocument` exposing only the rendered text and ticket ID. A static `TicketKnowledgeDocumentBuilder` will generate the canonical labeled string from a support ticket and its comments. Reusing the existing `SupportTicketAssigneeMapping` logic for assignee display avoids duplicating the UNASSIGNED constant and name formatting.

Decided against coupling the builder to the VO layer. Will either reuse `SupportTicketDetailVO.UNASSIGNED` or introduce a small shared constant in the rag package to avoid tight coupling.

The builder will live in the `rag` package. It will use a local `"UNASSIGNED"` constant and a small `assigneeDisplay` helper to render assignees without touching the VO layer.

Will reference `SupportTicketDetailVO.UNASSIGNED` directly because it is public. Status and priority will use raw enum names such as `OPEN` and `HIGH`. Comments will render as bullet points under a `Comments:` header, remaining empty when absent. Resolution information will appear under its own header when present.

Confirmed the exact nine-section labels from rag-ingestion.md. The builder will emit `Label: value` pairs separated by newlines. Empty resolution blocks will be omitted entirely, trimmed and checked with `isBlank()` before rendering.

The builder will sort comments internally by creation timestamp and ID to guarantee deterministic ordering. Null fields in the comparator will use `nullsLast` to avoid inventing content. Null comment lists will be treated as empty. Blank comment bodies will be skipped since the domain requires nonblank values. Considering whether the builder should be a Spring bean.

Decided on a plain final class with a `build` method instead of a Spring component. This keeps the builder lightweight and injectable later without annotations. Weighing two package options: `com.tothenew.bootcamp.rag.document` for future EMB-001 integration, or `com.tothenew.bootcamp.service.ticket.document` for proximity to the ticket service.

Decided to create the new `rag.document` package rather than placing the builder under `service.ticket`, since no `rag` layer exists yet and keeping indexing processor concerns separate is preferable. Started drafting the `StringBuilder` text rendering implementation.

Drafted the `StringBuilder` rendering loop. Each section appends a label and value, followed by a newline. Comments render as bullet points under their header. Resolution appears only when present. Decided to omit a trailing newline after the final section for cleaner deterministic equality.

The builder will emit a single newline after each section header. Empty Comments and Resolution blocks will render as bare headers without extra blank lines.

Confirmed the exact whitespace behavior: empty comments render as bare `Comments:` without trailing newlines, while resolution is omitted entirely when whitespace-only. Ready to implement the builder and run the focused tests.
</details></think>

## TASK-DOC-002 — Plan (review only)

### Objective / deps / IDs / done
- **Objective:** Add complete provenance/grounding metadata to every chunk input.
- **Depends on:** TASK-DOC-001 (canonical text unchanged).
- **IDs:** RAG-008–RAG-010 (`rag-ingestion.md` §3; RAG-010 also `requirements.md`).
- **Verify:** Metadata contract tests; exact `UNASSIGNED`; no missing required key.
- **Complete when:** Every document carries citation (`ticketId`) and stale-version provenance (`ticketVersion`).

### Required metadata (exact)
| Field | Type (proposed) | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `ticketId` | `Long` | `SupportTicket.getId()` |
| `ticketVersion` | `Long` | Inherited JPA `@Version` → `SupportTicket.getVersion()` (no extra knowledge-version field) |
| `chunkIndex` | `int` (zero-based) | **Contract in DOC-002; values set by EMB-001** when splitting |
| `status` | `SupportTicketStatus` (or enum `.name()` snapshot) | `ticket.getStatus()` |
| `priority` | `SupportTicketPriority` (or `.name()`) | `ticket.getPriority()` |
| `assigneeId` | `Long`, **nullable** | `assignee == null ? null : assignee.getId()` |
| `assigneeDisplay` | `String`, **never null** | `UNASSIGNED` or `User.getFullName()` (same as DOC-001 / VOs) |
| `category` | `String` | `ticket.getCategory()` |

Not in DOC-002: `documentId`, `indexedAt`, embeddings, content.

### Null / unassigned
- `assigneeId`: null when unassigned.
- `assigneeDisplay`: always present; literal **`UNASSIGNED`** when no assignee.
- Other listed fields required non-null on a persisted ticket (domain already enforces).

### `ticketVersion`
Snapshot of MySQL ticket optimistic-lock version at document build time; used later for stale-version / overwrite guards (architecture § ingestion; IDX owns enforcement).

### `chunkIndex` ownership
DOC-002 **defines** it as a required metadata key on the chunk-input contract and provides a way to stamp it (e.g. ticket-level snapshot + `withChunkIndex(n)`). DOC-002 does **not** compute chunk boundaries or indexes from text — **EMB-001** assigns `0..n-1`.

### Proposed models (immutable)
1. **`TicketDocumentMetadata`** — ticket-shared fields (`ticketId`…`category`, no/unspecified chunk yet), mapped from `SupportTicket`.
2. **`TicketChunkMetadata`** — full §3 set including `chunkIndex` (from (1) + index).
3. Optional envelope: **`TicketKnowledgeDocument` + ticket metadata** composition; **`content()` remains DOC-001 text byte-for-byte**.

### Attach without changing DOC-001
Compose beside the existing document; do not alter `TicketKnowledgeDocumentBuilder` / canonical string. Mapper reads `SupportTicket` (and may reuse document’s `ticketId` only as a consistency check).

### Minimum production surface
- Immutable metadata type(s) + mapper (`Document metadata mapper` per tasks.md).
- No Spring AI, PGVector, Ollama, indexing services.

### Minimum tests
- Assigned → non-null `assigneeId` + display = `fullName`.
- Unassigned → `assigneeId == null`, `assigneeDisplay == "UNASSIGNED"`.
- All required keys present; `ticketVersion` equals entity `@Version`.
- Status/priority/category/ticketId mapped correctly.
- Stamping `chunkIndex` does not change document text.
- Deterministic repeat for identical ticket state.

### Left for later
| Task | Owns |
|---|---|
| **EMB-001** | Chunking; assign real `chunkIndex`; size/overlap |
| **EMB-002** | Embeddings / Ollama abstraction |
| **IDX-*** | PGVector write, `documentId`/`indexedAt`, replace-by-version, re-ingestion |

### Domain mismatch
**None** for required fields. `SupportTicket` + `User` already supply id, version, status, priority, assignee, category; display convention matches existing VOs.

## TASK-EMB-001 — Plan (review only)

### Objective / IDs / deps / done
- **Objective:** Split one ticket document at a time with configurable boundary-aware chunking.
- **IDs:** RAG-002, RAG-010, NFR-001 (task); chunking also in `rag-ingestion.md` §4 / architecture §8.
- **Depends on:** DOC-002 (and thus DOC-001).
- **Complete when:** Size/overlap are **externalized** (not duplicated constants) and every chunk is attributable to **one** ticket.
- **Verify:** Boundary, overlap, long description/comment, deterministic indexes, empty-section (no empty chunks).

### Config (already present — reuse)
| Property | Default | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `bootcamp.support-ticket.rag.chunking.size` | **1600** | **characters** |
| `bootcamp.support-ticket.rag.chunking.overlap` | **200** | **characters** |

Bound to `SupportTicketRagProperties.Chunking` (`@Positive` size, `@Min(0)` overlap, `overlap < size`). Task’s 1600/200 match. **Do not hardcode duplicates.**

No `spec/rag-vector-store.md`; rules live in `.cursor/rules/rag-vector-store.mdc` (same intent).

### Proposed algorithm (one ticket only)
Input: DOC-001 `content` + DOC-002 `TicketDocumentMetadata` + chunking props.

1. Parse labeled DOC-001 text into segments on stable boundaries: section headers (`Ticket ID:`, `Title:`, …, `Comments:`, `Resolution Information:`) and comment lines (`- …`).
2. Pack segments greedily into chunks with `length ≤ size`, preferring not to break mid-segment.
3. If a single segment (e.g. long description/comment) exceeds `size`, hard-split that segment with **character** windows of `size` and advance by `size - overlap`.
4. Reject invalid config at chunker entry if props violate existing rules (size ≤ 0, overlap &lt; 0, overlap ≥ size).
5. Drop empty chunk bodies; never emit empty chunks.
6. Never mix tickets (one document → one chunk list).

### Section / boundary preservation
Prefer splits at labeled section and comment boundaries before mid-field cuts. DOC-001 string stays unchanged; chunker only reads it.

### Small document
If total (with identity prefix rules below) fits in one window → **single chunk**, `chunkIndex = 0`, full content.

### Long description / comments / resolution
Boundary pack first; oversized segments split with configured overlap. Same for resolution when present.

### Determinism & overlap
Same `(content, size, overlap)` → identical chunk texts and indexes. Overlap only on hard-splits of oversized segments (and optionally trailing window edges); packing order is document order.

### `chunkIndex` (DOC-002)
After producing ordered chunk texts `[0..n)`, stamp via `metadata.withChunkIndex(i)`. EMB-001 **assigns** indexes; DOC-002 only defines/stamps the field.

### Ticket identity per chunk
Per `rag-ingestion.md`: retain or **prepend** Ticket ID + Title on every chunk that does not already start with that document head, so retrieval context stays ticket-attributable. Header is part of chunk text; packing must keep final chunk length within `size` where feasible (trim body, not strip ID/title).

### Immutable chunk model
`TicketChunk` (or equivalent): `String text` + `TicketChunkMetadata` (full DOC-002 keys including `chunkIndex`).

### Minimum production surface
- `TicketChunk` (+ maybe list/result type)
- `TicketDocumentChunker` injecting/reading `SupportTicketRagProperties.getChunking()`
- No new size/overlap constants; no DOC-001/002 contract edits

### Minimum tests
Small doc → 1 chunk; section-boundary packing; hard-split + overlap on long description/comment; deterministic repeat; sequential `chunkIndex` 0..n-1; identity prefix on non-leading chunks; empty body not emitted; invalid size/overlap rejected; metadata fields preserved from DOC-002.

### Ownership
| Task | Owns |
|---|---|
| **EMB-001** | Chunk texts + stamped metadata indexes |
| **EMB-002** | Embeddings / Ollama abstraction |
| **IDX-*** | PGVector write/replace/versioning |

### Mismatches / assumptions
- **Units:** Task + properties = **characters**; spec allows tokenization “where feasible” — POC assumes characters (aligned with RIF config).
- **NFR-001** in `requirements.md` names top-K/threshold; EMB-001 task still cites it for externalized knobs — chunk size/overlap are already externalized under architecture §8.
- DOC-001 has no structured section offsets → chunker parses labeled text (no DOC-001 change needed).
- No blocker against current DOC-001/002 contracts.

### Files created

### Algorithm
1. Validate `size > 0`, `overlap >= 0`, `overlap < size`.
2. Extract identity prefix = `Ticket ID: …\nTitle: …\n`; fail if `prefix.length() >= size`.
3. Segment DOC-001 text on labeled sections; split Comments into header + each `\n- …` (join ≡ source).
4. Pack whole segments into body while `body + segment <= capacity` (`capacity = size` for chunk 0; `size - prefix.length()` after).
5. If an oversized segment starts an empty body → **hard-split** with windows of current/later capacity and **exact configured overlap** between windows only; no overlap during normal packing.
6. Chunk 0 = body only (already has identity); later chunks = `identityPrefix + body`.
7. Stamp `metadata.withChunkIndex(0..n-1)`; drop empty bodies.

### 1. Task contract (`spec/tasks.md`)
| | |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Replace all chunks for one ticket without partial/mixed versions |
| **IDs** | RAG-011–RAG-012, AC-010 |
| **Depends on** | EMB-002, RIF-002 |
| **Intent** | Embeddings **before** delete; **one PG transaction**: delete by `ticketId` then insert deterministic chunk IDs; keep prior index on failure |
| **Verify** | PGVector integration tests (replacement + injected add/delete failure) |
| **Done when** | Successful index holds **only one complete latest** ticket version |

### 2–3. Data flow (intended)
```
List<TicketEmbeddedChunk>  (text + TicketChunkMetadata + float[])
  → map to store rows (content + metadata JSON + embedding + deterministic id)
  → PG tx: DELETE all rows for ticketId → INSERT full set → commit
```
MySQL stays SoR; this path is **PostgreSQL-only** and must **not** join the MySQL ticket transaction (`architecture.md` dual-store / eventual consistency).

### 4. Metadata into PGVector
From `TicketChunkMetadata` into Document/metadata map (portable types):

| Key | Type |
|---|---|
| `ticketId` | `Long` / number |
| `ticketVersion` | `Long` |
| `chunkIndex` | `int` |
| `status` | `String` |
| `priority` | `String` |
| `assigneeId` | `Long` or omit/null |
| `assigneeDisplay` | `String` (`UNASSIGNED` when unassigned) |
| `category` | `String` |

`content` = chunk text. Optional `indexedAt` (data-model) can live in metadata JSON if desired—not in DOC-002 contract; open.

### 5. Deterministic IDs
Spec: unique vector `documentId`; unique intent `(ticketId, ticketVersion, chunkIndex)`.  
Task: “deterministic chunk IDs.” No exact string format prescribed.

**Propose (needs approval):**  
`documentId = "{ticketId}:{ticketVersion}:{chunkIndex}"`  
Requires **TEXT** id type on the Spring AI table (default RIF-002 builder uses **UUID**—not set today). Alternative: name-based UUID from that key without schema id-type change.

### 6. One indexing operation
Single call taking all `TicketEmbeddedChunk`s for one `ticketId` (+ same `ticketVersion`). Reject mixed ticket/version. Delete **all** existing rows for that `ticketId` (not only current version), then insert the new complete set (RAG-011 / AC-010).

### 7. Transaction boundary
- **PG:** `TransactionTemplate` on `SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure.getTransactionManager()` — delete+insert atomic.  
- **MySQL:** unchanged here; PENDING/INDEXED/FAILED and AFTER_COMMIT stay **IDX-003/004**.  
- Embed failure **before** delete (task + `rag-ingestion.md` §7). PG failure → rollback → prior vectors remain.

### 8. Ownership vs later IDX
| Task | Owns |
|---|---|
| **IDX-001** | PG replace adapter: precomputed vectors in, delete-by-ticketId + insert, PG tx, prior kept on failure |
| **IDX-002** | Stale-version guard (don’t overwrite newer indexed `@Version`) |
| **IDX-003** | AFTER_COMMIT → real `SupportTicketIndexingProcessor` (replace `NoOp`), MySQL PENDING→INDEXED/FAILED, NFR-004 |
| **IDX-004** | In-process retry / claim |

HUMAN REVIEW — TASK-IDX-001 PLAN APPROVED WITH ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS. IMPLEMENT IDX-001 ONLY.

The Spring AI 1.1.2 API finding is accepted:

PgVectorStore.add(List<Document>) re-embeds content and cannot consume EMB-002's precomputed float[].

Therefore:

1. APPROVED WRITE PATH

Use the dedicated RIF-002 PostgreSQL JDBC infrastructure for the IDX-001 write path.

Do NOT call PgVectorStore.add() for ingestion.

Use the already-computed embeddings from TicketEmbeddedChunk.

Keep the existing Spring AI PgVectorStore bean/configuration intact for schema initialization and later retrieval work.

Do not introduce another datasource.

2. ATOMIC REPLACEMENT

Given all TicketEmbeddedChunks for one ticket/version:

validate the complete input before touching PG;
embeddings already exist before replacement begins;
execute DELETE + all INSERTs inside ONE PostgreSQL transaction;
delete all existing vector rows for that ticketId;
insert the complete new chunk set;
commit only if all inserts succeed;
if delete/insert fails, rollback so the previously indexed complete version remains.

Do not involve the MySQL transaction.

3. DETERMINISTIC DOCUMENT ID

Keep the existing PGVector UUID id type.

Derive a deterministic UUID from the canonical identity:

ticketId:ticketVersion:chunkIndex

Use a stable UTF-8 byte representation and deterministic UUID generation.

Do NOT change the PGVector id column to TEXT.

Add tests proving:

same tuple → same UUID;
different ticket/version/chunkIndex → different UUIDs.

4. METADATA

Persist exactly:

ticketId
ticketVersion
chunkIndex
status
priority
assigneeId when assigned
assigneeDisplay
category

Preserve numeric/string types appropriately.

For an unassigned ticket, follow the PGVector/JSON representation supported by the current schema/API. Do not invent a fake numeric assignee ID. assigneeDisplay must remain UNASSIGNED.

Do NOT add indexedAt in IDX-001.

Content must be exactly TicketEmbeddedChunk.text().

Embedding must be exactly the precomputed TicketEmbeddedChunk.embedding().

5. INPUT INVARIANTS

Before DELETE, reject:

null/empty list;
null chunks;
mixed ticketId;
mixed ticketVersion;
duplicate chunkIndex;
non-sequential/missing chunk indexes if the current EMB contract requires 0..n-1;
null/invalid vectors;
vector dimension inconsistent with configured PGVector dimensions.

Validation failure must occur before any database mutation.

Do not re-embed.

6. JDBC / SPRING AI SCHEMA COMPATIBILITY

Before writing SQL, inspect the ACTUAL Spring AI 1.1.2 PGVector schema/table/column names and types produced by the current RIF-002 configuration.

Do not guess column names, metadata JSON type, vector binding syntax, or table name.

Reuse the configured table/schema values where available rather than duplicating them.

Ensure rows inserted through JDBC remain fully readable/searchable by the existing Spring AI PgVectorStore.

7. TRANSACTION

Use the dedicated PostgreSQL transaction manager from SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure.

DELETE and INSERT must participate in the same PG transaction.

Do not use the MySQL/JPA transaction manager.

8. TESTS

Add focused deterministic tests for:

mapping text/metadata/vector correctly;
deterministic UUID;
input validation;
mixed ticket/version rejection before mutation;
duplicate/missing indexes rejection where applicable;
wrong vector dimension rejection;
no EmbeddingModel invocation/re-embedding on write.

Add a real PGVector integration test using the project's existing Testcontainers infrastructure/pattern.

Integration test must prove:

A. initial indexing stores all chunks;

B. replacement for the same ticket removes the prior version and leaves only the complete new version;

C. another ticket's rows remain untouched;

D. injected INSERT failure after DELETE causes transaction rollback and preserves the previous complete ticket index;

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The target table is `public.vector_store`.

The table columns are id, content, metadata, and embedding. Inserts use ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE. UUID objects bind to id. PGvector handles the embedding column. Metadata deletes filter on ticketId via JSONB path.

Metadata filtering on ticketId may need bigint casting or exact JSONB containment. Unassigned assigneeId values should be omitted from the JSON map rather than set to null.

Deterministic UUIDs will use `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes` with an MD5 hash of `ticketId:ticketVersion:chunkIndex`. The indexer needs access to `TicketEmbeddedChunk`, which has a package-private constructor. The current options are placing the indexer in the `rag.embedding` package or adding a public factory method.

Adding a public factory or test helper to `TicketEmbeddedChunk` would alter the EMB-002 contract. Production code receives `TicketEmbeddedChunk` from outside, but tests still need to construct it. The indexer and its document ID utility will reside in the indexing package.

Unit tests will use Mockito-inline to mock the final `TicketEmbeddedChunk` directly. A public factory method on that class was rejected to preserve the EMB-002 contract.

`TicketChunkMetadata` also has a package-private constructor, so mocking it will require the same inline Mockito workaround.

Integration tests will run the full DOC-to-EMB-002 pipeline with a fake EmbeddingModel to generate real TicketEmbeddedChunk instances for the indexer.

Validation unit tests will avoid mocking package-private constructors by building chunks through the same pipeline with a stub embedder, keeping tests database-free and Spring-free.

Public UUID utilities will support deterministic-ID unit tests. Pipeline-driven construction also covers failure-injection tests without needing direct TicketEmbeddedChunk access.

The UUID generator will be a pure static utility taking ticketId, version, and chunkIndex directly, requiring no TicketEmbeddedChunk instance.

Implementation will proceed in four parts: the deterministic UUID utility, the replace indexer, unit tests, and Testcontainers integration tests.

The table name will reuse Spring AI’s PgVectorStore constants for schema and table name. The fully qualified name `public.vector_store` must be verified against the framework’s getFullyQualifiedTableName format.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Planning to use a simple JDBC DELETE statement for the PostgreSQL cleanup step.

Settled on a JSONB-based delete predicate using Jackson ObjectMapper to serialize metadata. Will use fully qualified table names and default schema/table constants. UUID conversion via setObject. Both CREATE and INSERT use jsonb casting.

Designing a RecordingEmbeddingModel to verify the EmbeddingModel is never invoked during indexing. Chunk validation will enforce sequential indices 0 through n-1. The replace method will use explicit PG transaction manager instead of @Transactional, wrapping operations in TransactionTemplate.

The replace method will delete existing vectors by ticketId, then insert the new chunks within the explicit transaction block. For the injected INSERT failure test, a JdbcTemplate wrapper or a custom indexer test double is preferred over a simple spy. The rollback scenario will index version 1 of a ticket, force a mid-insert failure during version 2 replacement, and assert that version 1 data remains intact.

Rejected adding test hooks to the production indexer. The simplest integration test approach is a JdbcTemplate wrapper that fails on the Nth insert. Overriding insertBatch in a test subclass is another option. Dimension mismatches and unique constraints were considered but rejected because validation occurs before deletion.

Reflection was rejected. The integration test will use TransactionTemplate directly to prove the DELETE-and-fail-rollback pattern matches the indexer. A test subclass of TicketVectorIndexer will be used to simulate the mid-insert failure.

Will make `insertRows` protected so a test subclass can override it to inject a failure. The indexer will carry `@Service` and `@ConditionalOnBean(SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure.class)` so it only registers when PostgreSQL JDBC infrastructure is present; without credentials, no bean is created.

Unit tests will avoid Docker entirely. They will mock JdbcTemplate and TransactionManager, and use a fixed embedding model to build TicketEmbeddedChunk instances. Pure UUID tests will remain separate. Validation tests will call replace with invalid input, assert exceptions, and verify JDBC is never invoked.

Mocked TransactionManager will return a fixed TransactionStatus and leave commit and rollback no-ops. This lets TransactionTemplate.execute invoke the callback directly without real transactions. Unit tests will verify the DELETE statement is issued against the correct ticketId.

The indexer intentionally carries no EmbeddingModel dependency, so unit tests will verify the embedding model receives zero invocations. Integration tests will use a RecordingEmbeddingModel as the primary bean to confirm the indexer never triggers it. Also verifying that Document IDs are valid UUID strings before conversion to PostgreSQL types.

Metadata serialization will use a LinkedHashMap to guarantee stable key ordering. Null assigneeId values will be omitted from the JSONB payload. The implementation is ready to begin. Spring’s ObjectMapper will correctly emit Long values as numbers. Integration tests will later read vectors back via PgVectorStore.similaritySearch, though that path will invoke EmbeddingModel for query generation.

Will verify indexed content and embedding dimensions via direct JDBC SELECT queries rather than PgVectorStore similarity search. The insert statement will use ON CONFLICT to match Spring AI compatibility. Fully qualified table names will be built from PgVectorStore schema and table constants.
</details></think>

# TASK-IDX-002 — Implementation Plan (PLAN ONLY)

**Status:** Specification / planning — **not implemented**. STOP for human review.  
**Baseline:** IDX-001 committed at `24015ade86bdd0f0379c22119b4a23f25ad173d7`.

---

## 1. TASK-IDX-002 contract (from `spec/tasks.md`)

| Field | Spec text |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Stop delayed work from overwriting a newer indexed JPA version. |
| **IDs** | **RAG-012**, **AC-010** |
| **Affected** | Indexing-state comparison and PGVector version checks |
| **Depends on** | TASK-IDX-001, TASK-SVC-002 |
| **Intent** | Compare requested/current/indexed `SupportTicket.@Version`; abandon stale work; only mark INDEXED when request is still current. |
| **Verify** | Out-of-order concurrency test where V+1 completes before V. |
| **Complete when** | **V can never replace an already indexed V+1.** |

### Requirement / AC / NFR IDs (authoritative)

| ID | Text / role for IDX-002 |
|---|---|
| **RAG-012** | Delayed ingestion for an older ticket version must not overwrite a newer indexed version. |
| **AC-010** | Successful re-ingestion leaves no old chunks or old metadata for that ticket (IDX-001 + fence preserves that success condition under races). |
| **RAG-011** | Complete replacement (already IDX-001); IDX-002 must not weaken it. |
| Supporting (not owned by IDX-002 write path) | FR-021–FR-023, AC-008–AC-009, NFR-004–NFR-005 — MySQL intent / after-commit / FAILED lifecycle → **IDX-003+** |

### Algorithmic home in `rag-ingestion.md` §7

For requested version `V`:

| Step | Spec action | IDX owner |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | If MySQL current version newer than `V`, abandon `V` | **IDX-003** |
| 5–9 | Begin PG tx → **verify `V` is not older than currently indexed `@Version`** → DELETE → INSERT → commit | **IDX-001 + IDX-002** |
| 10 | Mark MySQL `INDEXED` only if `V` remains requested | **IDX-003** |

`architecture.md` §4 step 7 matches: replace in one PG transaction **only if it cannot overwrite a newer indexed version**.

### Completion condition (exact)

After IDX-002: for any ticket, if PGVector already holds a complete index at version **V+1** (or higher), a later attempt to apply version **V** must **not** change those rows (no DELETE/INSERT of V). Concurrent V and V+1 must not finish with V as the surviving index.

---

## 2. Current-state analysis

### Authoritative ticket version

- **Authoritative knowledge version:** `SupportTicket` inherited JPA `@Version` (`BaseEntity.version`) — `rag-ingestion.md` §3/§5; `data-model.md`; no separate knowledge-version field.
- **Chunk provenance:** `TicketChunkMetadata.ticketVersion` / PG metadata `ticketVersion` — same `@Version` snapshot.
- **MySQL intent:** `TicketIndexingState.requestedVersion` / `indexedVersion` — also `@Version` values (SVC-002 exists; processor is still `NoOpSupportTicketIndexingProcessor`).

### What IDX-001 stores today

- Table: `public.vector_store` (Spring AI 1.1.2 defaults).
- Metadata JSON includes `ticketVersion` (= batch’s JPA `@Version`).
- One PG tx: DELETE by `ticketId` + UPSERT all chunks; **no version comparison, no lock**.
- Public API: `void replaceTicketVectors(List<TicketEmbeddedChunk>)` — always mutates after validate.

### Version comparisons that exist elsewhere

- SVC-002 records `requestedVersion` and publishes AFTER_COMMIT events; **does not** fence PGVector.
- No code today reads max PG `ticketVersion` before replace.

---

## 3. Stale-version race being prevented

**Canonical race (tasks.md verify + RAG-012):**

1. Indexing for ticket knowledge **V=5** starts (embed offline).
2. Ticket mutates; **V=6** indexing starts and **completes** (PG holds only v6).
3. Delayed **V=5** later calls replace.
4. **Forbidden end state:** PG regresses to v5 (or mixed v5/v6).

**Concurrency strengthening of the same bug:**

- TxA (v5) and TxB (v6) both pass a check-then-act without serialization → last commit wins → **v5 can win after v6**.

IDX-002’s job is the **PGVector side** of that guarantee (step 6 + race-safe apply). MySQL “abandon if current > V” and “mark INDEXED” remain orchestration.

---

## 4. Choice among A / B / C / D (from specs, not preference)

| Option | Meaning | Spec fit for IDX-002 |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Read indexed `ticketVersion` from PG **inside the same PG tx**; refuse if `incoming < indexed` | **Required** — `rag-ingestion.md` §7 step 6; architecture §4 step 7 |
| **B** | Compare to live MySQL `SupportTicket.@Version` | **Not sufficient alone** for PG regression; belongs to **step 2 / IDX-003**. MySQL can be at v7 while PG is at v6; fencing must use **indexed** (PG), not “current ticket”. |
| **C** | Both inside IDX-002 | Spec splits them across steps 2 vs 6; bundling MySQL reads into IDX-002 pulls IDX-003 scope |
| **D** | Other mechanism | **Advisory lock (or equivalent critical section)** is required to make **A** race-safe; it is the **locking strategy**, not a replacement for the version check |

**Proposed ownership answer:** IDX-002 = **A + D** (PG indexed-version fence under a per-ticket PG critical section). **B** and “mark INDEXED only if still current” stay **IDX-003**.

**Note on tasks.md Intent wording** (“Compare requested/current/indexed… only mark INDEXED…”): that sentence spans the full ingestion pipeline. Per user boundary rules and IDX-003’s assignment of AFTER_COMMIT / MySQL lifecycle, treat **mark INDEXED** and **MySQL current-vs-V abandon** as **out of IDX-002** unless human overrides. IDX-002 still enables that pipeline by returning a clear **APPLIED vs REJECTED_STALE** outcome.

---

## 5. Proposed concurrency / version-fencing algorithm

Extend the IDX-001 write path (same PG `TransactionTemplate` / `SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure` TM):

```
validate(chunks) → incoming V, ticketId   // unchanged; before any mutation

BEGIN PG TRANSACTION  (existing DataSourceTransactionManager)
  1. pg_advisory_xact_lock(<stable key derived from ticketId>)
     // transaction-scoped; released on commit/rollback

  2. indexedMax = SELECT MAX((metadata->>'ticketVersion')::bigint)
                 FROM public.vector_store
                 WHERE (metadata->>'ticketId')::bigint = ticketId

  3. IF indexedMax IS NOT NULL AND incoming V < indexedMax THEN
        // abandon: no DELETE, no INSERT
        COMMIT (or rollback empty) → return REJECTED_STALE
     END IF

  4. ELSE
        DELETE all rows for ticketId          // IDX-001
        INSERT/UPSERT complete chunk set      // IDX-001
        COMMIT → return APPLIED
     END IF
END
```

**API evolution (smallest necessary):** change/replace `void` with a result such as:

- `TicketVectorReplaceResult.APPLIED`
- `TicketVectorReplaceResult.REJECTED_STALE`

so IDX-003 can avoid treating stale abandon as FAILED / INDEXED incorrectly. Prefer evolving `TicketVectorIndexer.replaceTicketVectors` (same class IDX-001) over a parallel unchecked path.

**Do not** call `PgVectorStore.add`; do not re-embed; do not touch MySQL.

### Why `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` alone is insufficient

- With **no rows**, `FOR UPDATE` locks nothing → two first-writers both see “absent” and race.
- After DELETE in the same tx, row locks on old versions are gone before INSERT completes for waiters in awkward interleavings.
- Spec’s unique `(ticketId, ticketVersion, chunkIndex)` is **intent only**; Spring AI table has **UUID PK only** — no natural mutex row.

### Why advisory xact lock (preferred smallest mechanism)

- No new table / migration.
- Serializes all replace attempts per `ticketId` for the duration of the PG tx.
- Works when the table is empty.
- Released automatically on commit/rollback (no unlock leak on failure).
- Compatible with IDX-001 DELETE+UPSERT inside the **same** tx after the check.

**Stable lock key:** e.g. `pg_advisory_xact_lock(42 /* namespace */, ticketId)` (document the constant). Avoid `hashtext` collisions across unrelated keys if using single-arg form.

**Alternative (larger):** `ticket_vector_fence(ticket_id PK, indexed_version)` with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE excluded.version >= fence.version` — only needed if advisory locks are rejected; report as optional escalation, not first choice.

---

## 6. Proof sketch (race-safe under real PostgreSQL)

Assume two txs for same `ticketId`, isolation READ COMMITTED (Spring default):

| Time | Tx_old (V=5) | Tx_new (V=6) |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | acquires advisory lock | blocks on same lock |
| T2 | reads indexedMax (null or ≤5); applies v5; commits; **releases lock** | |
| T3 | | acquires lock; reads indexedMax=5; 6≥5; applies v6; commits |
| End | | PG = v6 |

| Time | Tx_new (V=6) first | Tx_old (V=5) delayed |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | lock → apply v6 → commit | waiting |
| T2 | | lock → indexedMax=6 → **5 < 6** → REJECTED_STALE; no DELETE |

**TOCTOU without lock fails:** both read indexedMax=null (or both read 4), both pass, commit order v6 then v5 → regression. Advisory lock makes the check+mutate **atomic w.r.t. other IDX writers for that ticket**.

Equal-version concurrent retries: serialized; second APPLIED is idempotent replace of same V (allowed: “not older”).

---

## 7. PostgreSQL transaction / locking strategy

- **TM:** `SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure.getTransactionManager()` only.
- **Lock:** `pg_advisory_xact_lock` before version read.
- **Check + DELETE + INSERT:** same transaction (IDX-001 invariant).
- **Stale path:** no mutation; commit empty / return REJECTED_STALE (rows unchanged).
- **Failure after DELETE:** existing IDX-001 rollback still holds (injected INSERT failure tests remain valid **after** lock+check).
- **No MySQL tx** participation.

---

## 8. Behavior matrix

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| No PG rows | `indexedMax` null → **APPLIED** (first index) |
| `incoming > indexed` | **APPLIED** (replace) |
| `incoming == indexed` | **APPLIED** (idempotent full replace; “not older”) |
| `incoming < indexed` | **REJECTED_STALE**; zero row changes |
| Multiple chunks same ticket/version | Unchanged IDX-001 validation (0..n-1, single version) |
| Malformed / mixed versions for one ticket | Use **MAX(ticketVersion)** for fence (conservative vs regression). **Open:** optionally fail closed if `COUNT(DISTINCT ticketVersion) > 1` before apply — recommend log + proceed with MAX for POC unless human wants hard fail |
| Concurrent same ticket | Serialized by advisory lock; older cannot win after newer |
| Other ticketId | Different lock key; isolation unchanged |
| IDX-001 INSERT failure after DELETE | Full rollback; prior complete index remains; fence lock released |

---

## 9. Relationship to IDX-001

- Reuse table, SQL UPSERT shape, validation, deterministic UUIDs, metadata map, dimensions check.
- Fencing wraps the existing mutate block; does not bypass validation.
- **Contract change:** return result enum (necessary for IDX-003). Update IDX-001 unit/IT call sites to assert `APPLIED`.
- Do not weaken atomic DELETE+INSERT.

---

## 10. Unit tests (deterministic)

Focus on fencing logic (mock JDBC / spy indexer):

1. First index (null max) → APPLIED; DELETE+INSERT invoked.
2. Newer replaces older → APPLIED.
3. Equal version → APPLIED.
4. Older → REJECTED_STALE; **no** DELETE/INSERT.
5. Validation failures still happen **before** lock/mutate (IDX-001).
6. Advisory lock SQL / ordering: lock → select max → mutate (verify call order).
7. No `EmbeddingModel` on replace path (retain IDX-001 proof).

---

## 11. Real PGVector concurrency / integration tests

**Required:** yes — tasks.md verify is an out-of-order concurrency test; IDX-002 is a transaction guarantee. Prefer Testcontainers PostgreSQL+pgvector (reuse IDX-001 IT pattern; fixed EmbeddingModel; no Ollama).

Minimum scenarios:

| # | Scenario |
|---|---|
| A | First index succeeds |
| B | Newer replaces older; only new version remains |
| C | Equal-version re-index leaves that version complete |
| D | Older after newer → REJECTED_STALE; prior rows unchanged (content/metadata/ids) |
| E | Injected INSERT failure after DELETE still rolls back (IDX-001) under fenced path |
| F | **Concurrent:** start two threads (or two txs) applying V and V+1 with barrier so both race; after both finish, PG must be **V+1 only** (never V) |
| G | Other ticket untouched |
| H | EmbeddingModel call count unchanged during replace |

---

## 12. Expected files to create/change (when implementing)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `TicketVectorIndexer.java` | Advisory lock + max-version check; return result |
| New small type e.g. `TicketVectorReplaceResult.java` | APPLIED / REJECTED_STALE |
| Possibly extract lock-key helper | package-private |
| `TicketVectorIndexerTest.java` | Fence cases + update for result type |
| `TicketVectorIndexerIT.java` or new `TicketVectorIndexerVersionFenceIT.java` | Concurrency + matrix |
| **Do not** change DOC/EMB contracts, SVC-002 processor, MySQL entities, retrieval |

---

## 13. Spec / code mismatches

1. **tasks.md Intent** mentions mark INDEXED / current version abandon — **pipeline-wide**; IDX-003 owns MySQL side.
2. **data-model.md** wants unique `(ticketId, ticketVersion, chunkIndex)` and `indexedAt` — Spring AI schema lacks those; IDX-001 omitted `indexedAt`; unique constraint **not** available as mutex.
3. **IDX-001** always replaces — without fencing, RAG-012 is open; IDX-002 closes it.
4. Processor still **no-op** — fine; IDX-002 does not wire AFTER_COMMIT.

---

## 14. Open decisions / blockers

| Item | Severity | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Advisory lock vs fence table | **Decision** | Prefer `pg_advisory_xact_lock`; no schema change |
| Return type vs exception on stale | **Decision** | Return `REJECTED_STALE` (abandon ≠ failure) |
| Equal-version = apply | **Decision** | Apply (matches “not older”) |
| Mixed legacy versions | **Decision** | Fence on MAX; optional hard-fail |
| tasks.md “mark INDEXED” in IDX-002 | **Boundary** | Defer to IDX-003 unless human pulls it in |
| MySQL `@Version` check in IDX-002 | **Boundary** | Defer to IDX-003 (step 2) |
| Change `void` API | **Necessary** | Smallest compliant contract evolution |

**BLOCKER?** Not if advisory locks (or a fence table) are allowed. **Race-safe IDX-002 is impossible with check-then-act alone on `vector_store`.** Smallest compliant addition: **transaction-scoped advisory lock** — no migration. Escalate to fence table only if advisory locks are rejected.

## 15. Explicit IDX-002 vs IDX-003 / IDX-004 boundary

| Concern | Owner |
|---|---|
| PG indexed-version fence + race-safe replace | **IDX-002** |
| Atomic DELETE+INSERT primitive | **IDX-001** (extended by 002) |
| AFTER_COMMIT listener → real processor; load ticket/comments; step 2 abandon if MySQL current > V; embed; call indexer; mark INDEXED/FAILED; replace NoOp | **IDX-003** |
| Claim PENDING/FAILED; retry; max attempts; concurrent claim | **IDX-004** |
| Soft-delete chunk removal | Later / soft-delete trigger path (not IDX-002) |
| Retrieval / `/api/ai/ask` / citations | RET/GEN/CIT |

2. `incoming == indexed` → re-apply allowed.
3. Lock namespace constant is process-local convention documented in code.
4. No change to Spring AI table DDL for IDX-002.

The reviewed plan is approved with these architectural decisions:

   The lock, indexed-version check, DELETE, and INSERT/UPSERT must all occur

   SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure PostgreSQL transaction manager.

4. Required ordering:

   validate incoming batch completely
   → BEGIN PG transaction
   → acquire per-ticket advisory transaction lock
   → read currently indexed ticket version
   → compare incoming version
   → if stale: perform NO DELETE/INSERT
   → otherwise execute existing IDX-001 atomic replacement
   → commit

5. Stale definition:

   incomingVersion < indexedVersion
       => REJECTED_STALE

   No vector rows:
       => APPLIED

   incomingVersion > indexedVersion:
       => APPLIED

   incomingVersion == indexedVersion:
       => APPLIED

6. Introduce a small explicit result contract such as:

   TicketVectorReplaceResult.APPLIED
   TicketVectorReplaceResult.REJECTED_STALE

8. Mixed/corrupt existing PG versions clarification:

   Do NOT silently repair a ticket whose existing PGVector rows contain
   multiple distinct ticketVersion values.

   While holding the advisory lock, detect inconsistent existing versions
   for that ticket.

   If more than one distinct indexed ticketVersion exists, FAIL CLOSED with
   a clear exception and make NO DELETE/INSERT changes.

   The transaction must leave the existing rows unchanged.

   This is an invariant violation, not REJECTED_STALE.

Two advisory lock strategies are being compared: a single bigint key or a two-integer pair with a namespace constant. The two-integer approach is preferred because ticket IDs are typically small enough to fit safely within the integer range.

The two-integer advisory lock syntax is being drafted for JDBC execution. Complex bigint packing was rejected as too unwieldy. A namespace constant and a `hashtextextended` alternative are now under consideration.

The advisory lock implementation will use a two-integer key. The namespace constant is set to 0x49445832 ("IDX2"). Ticket IDs will be cast to int via Math.toIntExact. This assumes POC ticket IDs remain small enough to fit safely within the signed int4 range.

A concrete `acquireTicketLock` method is being drafted. It validates that the ticket ID fits within the signed int4 advisory lock key range and throws an exception if the value exceeds the bounds. A single bigint lock key alternative is also being considered as a fallback.

Indexed version queries will read distinct ticketVersion values from the vector store metadata. A count greater than one triggers a failure to enforce the indexed-version fence. Zero matches means no indexed version exists. One match returns that version. A single-count aggregate query is also being considered as an alternative.

An IllegalStateException with a clear message will serve as the version-fence exception. The transaction template will return TicketVectorReplaceResult.APPLIED. The advisory lock call will use `jdbcTemplate.execute` with a `ConnectionCallback` rather than `queryForObject`, since the lock returns no meaningful value and the callback pattern is cleaner for a void-returning operation.

A simpler `jdbcTemplate.query` pattern is being weighed against the `execute` callback for acquiring the advisory lock.

The indexed-version query will select distinct `ticketVersion` values from the vector store metadata. A null `ticketVersion` in the metadata is flagged as a potential corruption issue.

Clarifying the concurrency test strategy. A sequential stale test is simpler: the new version finishes first, then the old version is rejected as stale. True concurrent races are harder to prove because without the advisory lock, either thread could win. The lock must ensure serialization so the higher version always wins.

The concurrency proof relies on the advisory lock ordering transactions. If both threads start with an empty table, whichever acquires the lock first applies its version. The second thread then either upgrades to the newer version or rejects as stale. The final state must always be the highest version, never a lone older version. The implementation will use a CyclicBarrier to synchronize both threads before they begin, and a CountDownLatch to signal completion.

### Test results
| Suite | Count | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (`TicketVectorIndexerTest` + `TicketVectorDocumentIdsTest`) | **13** (11+2) | PASS |
| PGVector IT (`TicketVectorIndexerIT`) | **3** | PASS |

### Files
| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `TicketVectorReplaceResult.java` | **Created** — `APPLIED` / `REJECTED_STALE` |
| `TicketVectorIndexer.java` | **Modified** — fence + advisory lock |
| `TicketVectorIndexerTest.java` | **Modified** — IDX-002 unit coverage |
| `TicketVectorIndexerIT.java` | **Modified** — A–I + real concurrency |

### Production changes to IDX-001
`replaceTicketVectors` now returns `TicketVectorReplaceResult`. Inside the same PG tx (`SupportTicketPgVectorJdbcInfrastructure` TM):

1. `pg_advisory_xact_lock(0x49445832, ticketId)`
2. `SELECT DISTINCT ticketVersion` — fail closed if >1 distinct
3. if `incoming < indexed` → `REJECTED_STALE` (no DELETE/INSERT)
4. else existing DELETE + UPSERT → `APPLIED`

Unchanged: precomputed embeddings, deterministic UUIDs, metadata, no `PgVectorStore.add`, no MySQL TM.

### Concurrency proof (IT F)
Two threads share a `CyclicBarrier`, then each runs `replaceTicketVectors` for **V=5** and **V=6** on the same ticket via independent pool connections/transactions. After both finish: **only version 6** remains, V6 is `APPLIED`, V5 is `APPLIED` or `REJECTED_STALE`. Without the advisory lock, last-writer-wins could leave V=5; serialization + fence prevents that.

Sufficient context has been gathered to draft the IDX-003 plan.

Reusing the existing AFTER_COMMIT TransactionalEventListener instead of inventing a new hook. The NoOp placeholder must become a real @Component implementing SupportTicketIndexingProcessor, requiring @Primary or removal of the NoOp bean. Soft-delete handling is deferred because the product write API does not exist yet; the open decision is whether to stub the soft-delete path or only handle the load of a deleted ticket.

The PROCESSING status enum exists but is never set. FR-023 and architecture step 8 mark INDEXED or FAILED. rag-ingestion assigns PROCESSING when a worker claims a ticket, which belongs to IDX-004. For the AFTER_COMMIT path, IDX-003 could briefly set PROCESSING at the start of process() or skip it entirely. The open decision is whether to set PROCESSING without claim semantics or leave it for IDX-004.

IDX-003 will set PROCESSING at the start of each attempt for visibility, then mark INDEXED or FAILED in a separate MySQL transaction. IDX-004 will handle claims and concurrency for retries. If a newer version is requested during processing, the current attempt should abandon the older version rather than mark it INDEXED.

When the requested version is stale, the processor returns immediately without marking INDEXED. A newer event will fire automatically, so recursive chaining within the same call is unnecessary.

Before marking INDEXED, the processor must re-read TicketIndexingState inside the MySQL transaction to confirm the version still matches the requested version after PostgreSQL succeeds.

A stale PostgreSQL version triggers REJECTED_STALE and must be abandoned, not marked FAILED. The AFTER_COMMIT listener runs synchronously on the publishing thread, satisfying the no-async requirement. Verification will use test doubles for PostgreSQL and Ollama to avoid live infrastructure, covering trigger matrix, rollback, and outage scenarios. The processor must tolerate missing TicketVectorIndexer or EmbeddingModel beans by marking the record FAILED, per NFR-004.

The pipeline chains repository lookups, document building, chunking, embedding, and vector indexing. The processor class will be DefaultSupportTicketIndexingProcessor or RagSupportTicketIndexingProcessor. The NoOp placeholder must be removed or excluded via @ConditionalOnMissingBean. A sanitize helper for lastError is also needed.

Unit and integration tests will use Testcontainers for MySQL and PostgreSQL plus a FixedEmbeddingModel. The soft-delete trigger is absent from the ticket service. The PROCESSING status is unused. The plan will abandon stale versions rather than recursively process the newest one.
</details></think>

# TASK-IDX-003 — Plan Only

**Baseline:** IDX-002 @ `2229767962000da6db14485f0ad2518b986d3a88`  
**Status:** Planning only — no implementation.

---

## 1. Contract (`spec/tasks.md`)

| Field | Spec |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Start embedding/indexing only after committed MySQL changes |
| **IDs** | FR-021–FR-023, AC-008–AC-009, NFR-004–NFR-005 |
| **Depends on** | IDX-002, SVC-002 |
| **Intent** | Process PENDING after commit; failed embedding/PG → FAILED without changing ticket; triggers match `rag-ingestion.md` |
| **Verify** | Trigger matrix, rollback, PG outage, model outage, terminal-rejection |
| **Complete when** | Every searchable trigger covered; ticket writes survive downstream failure |

---

## 2. Current wiring (reuse — do not replace)

**AFTER_COMMIT already exists (SVC-002):**

```
SupportTicketService searchable write
  → SupportTicketIndexingIntentService.recordSearchableChange
      (same MySQL tx: PENDING + requestedVersion + publish event)
  → commit
  → SupportTicketIndexingRequestedListener
      (@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT))
  → SupportTicketIndexingProcessor.process(ticketId, requestedVersion)
      → currently NoOpSupportTicketIndexingProcessor
```

**Proof indexing cannot run before commit:** listener is `TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT` only; rollback test already in `SupportTicketMysqlIntegrationTest`. IDX-003 keeps this hook; **no second event bus**.

**Invocation site:** only `SupportTicketIndexingRequestedListener`. Replace by registering a real `@Component` implementing `SupportTicketIndexingProcessor` and removing/`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` the NoOp. Existing MySQL ITs already `@Primary`-override with `RecordingSupportTicketIndexingProcessor` — preserve that pattern.

**Execution model:** default Spring `TransactionalEventListener` is **synchronous on the calling thread after commit**. Spec/architecture describe in-process after-commit processing with no broker/executor. **Do not invent async** unless human overrides.

---

## 3. Proposed end-to-end orchestration (compose existing beans)

For event `(ticketId, V)` after commit:

1. **New MySQL tx (short):** load `TicketIndexingState`; if `requestedVersion != V` → abandon (newer supersedes). Optionally set `PROCESSING` + `lastAttemptAt` + bump `attemptCount` *(open: see §E)*.
2. **Load SoR:** `SupportTicket` + `findByTicketIdOrdered` comments + assignee (same APIs `SupportTicketService` already uses for detail). Soft-deleted → soft-delete vector cleanup path *(open)*.
3. If ticket `@Version` **> V** → abandon (do not INDEX for V); newest PENDING already has/will get its own AFTER_COMMIT.
4. If ticket `@Version` **< V** → invariant violation → FAILED (sanitized).
5. If `@Version == V`:  
   DOC-001 → DOC-002 → EMB-001 → EMB-002 → `TicketVectorIndexer.replaceTicketVectors`.
6. **PG result:**
   - `APPLIED` → new MySQL tx: if `requestedVersion` still `V` → `INDEXED`, `indexedVersion=V`, clear `lastError`; else abandon (do not INDEX old V).
   - `REJECTED_STALE` → abandon (not FAILED); PG already has newer.
7. Any DOC/EMB/PG exception → new MySQL tx: `FAILED` + sanitized `lastError`; **never** touch ticket row / business data.

Ticket write tx and indexing MySQL updates are **separate**; PG uses dedicated PG TM only (IDX-001/002).

---

## 4. Version / state transition table

| Situation | MySQL ticket | Indexing state action | PG |
|---|---|---|---|
| Searchable write commits | `@Version=V` | `PENDING`, `requestedVersion=V` (SVC-002) | — |
| AFTER_COMMIT starts for V | — | optional `PROCESSING` | — |
| Current ticket `@Version` > V | unchanged | leave PENDING for newer / no INDEX for V | no write for V |
| `REJECTED_STALE` | unchanged | no INDEX for V | unchanged (IDX-002) |
| Embed/PG/DOC failure | unchanged | `FAILED` + sanitized error | prior complete index kept |
| `APPLIED` and `requestedVersion` still V | unchanged | `INDEXED`, `indexedVersion=V` | V rows only |
| `APPLIED` but `requestedVersion` now > V | unchanged | **do not** set INDEXED for V | V may sit until newer run |
| Old V must never mark newer INDEXED | — | INDEXED only if `requestedVersion==V` at mark time | fence already in IDX-002 |

**Authoritative version:** ticket JPA `@Version` (= metadata `ticketVersion` = intent versions).

---

## 5. Failure matrix (IDX-003)

| Failure | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Ticket load / missing | FAILED (or abandon if soft-deleted + handled) |
| DOC/chunk | FAILED |
| Embedding / Ollama | FAILED; no PG delete |
| PG / inconsistent versions exception | FAILED; ticket intact |
| `REJECTED_STALE` | Abandon, not FAILED |
| Ticket advanced during processing | Abandon INDEX for old V |
| Soft-delete | Spec: delete all chunks + record handled — **no product soft-delete write API yet** (deferred); see blockers |

---

## 6. IDX-003 vs IDX-004

| IDX-003 | IDX-004 |
|---|---|
| Real processor on existing AFTER_COMMIT | Explicit retry/claim of PENDING/FAILED |
| One-shot process of committed V | Concurrent claim, max attempts, backoff policy |
| Mark INDEXED/FAILED for this attempt | Re-invoke processing safely |
| Trigger coverage for searchable writes | Fail-then-success / newest-version retry tests |

---

## 7. Load requirements (no DOC contract change)

Reuse:

- `SupportTicketRepositoryService` active ticket load (+ soft-delete decision)
- `SupportTicketCommentRepositoryService.findByTicketIdOrdered`
- Assignee already on ticket entity / mapper

Compose: `TicketKnowledgeDocumentBuilder` → `TicketDocumentMetadataMapper` → `TicketDocumentChunker` → `TicketChunkEmbeddingService` → `TicketVectorIndexer`.

---

## 8. Tests (minimum)

**Unit:** processor orchestration with mocks — AFTER_COMMIT not re-tested as mechanism (already SVC-002); version abandon; INDEXED guard; FAILED on embed/PG; `REJECTED_STALE` ≠ FAILED; no duplicate embed/write logic.

**IT (MySQL Testcontainers + PGVector + FixedEmbeddingModel — mirror IDX-001/002):**  
AFTER_COMMIT only after commit; rollback → no process; happy path → INDEXED + vectors; embed fail → FAILED, ticket intact; PG fail → FAILED; version bump before process → old V not INDEXED; stale PG → abandon; other ticket isolated.

**Live Ollama E2E smoke:** **not required by IDX-003.** IDX-003 verify = trigger/rollback/outage (doubles OK). Live MySQL→PG→retrieve→generate = **TASK-E2E-002** (depends on UI/EVL/IDX-004). Ollama establish = **RIF-003**.

---

## 9. Expected files

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| Create | Real `*SupportTicketIndexingProcessor` (name TBD) |
| Create | Optional small `IndexingErrorSanitizer` / state updater helper |
| Modify | Remove or `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` `NoOpSupportTicketIndexingProcessor` |
| Create | Processor unit tests |
| Create | Pipeline IT (MySQL+PG+fixed EmbeddingModel) |
| Touch carefully | Existing MySQL IT `@Primary` recording config must still override |

**Do not modify:** DOC/EMB contracts, IDX-001/002 fence logic (call only), retrieval/API.

---

## 10. Mismatches / blockers

1. **Soft-delete indexing** specified in `rag-ingestion.md` §5/§7; **no soft-delete write API** — defer full path; decide minimal “ticket already deleted at process time” behavior.
2. **`PROCESSING`:** enum exists; never written. IDX-004 owns claim; IDX-003 may set PROCESSING for visibility or leave PENDING until INDEXED/FAILED — **needs human choice**.
3. **Step 2 “process newest”:** AFTER_COMMIT already fires per newest write; prefer **abandon old V** over recursive re-entry.
4. **Conditional beans:** `TicketVectorIndexer` / `EmbeddingModel` may be absent → mark FAILED (NFR-004), do not break ticket APIs.
5. **NoOp removal vs tests:** keep `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` or tests continue `@Primary` override.

---

# End summary

### A. Flow
Commit → existing AFTER_COMMIT listener → real processor → load ticket/comments → version gate → DOC→EMB→IDX-002 → MySQL INDEXED/FAILED/abandon in **separate** MySQL txs.

### B. State/version
PENDING (write tx) → [optional PROCESSING] → INDEXED iff PG `APPLIED` and `requestedVersion` still V; else FAILED on infra/errors; abandon on MySQL-newer or `REJECTED_STALE`.

### C. Files
New processor (+ helper/tests/IT); retire NoOp conditionally; no DOC/EMB/IDX fence rewrites.

### D. Verification
Unit + MySQL/PG Testcontainers with fixed embeddings; trigger/rollback/outage/version; not live Ollama E2E (E2E-002).

### E. Open decisions
1. Set `PROCESSING` in IDX-003 or only IDX-004?  
2. Soft-delete-at-process-time: delete vectors now vs FAILED/no-op until delete API exists?  
3. Bean wiring: replace NoOp vs `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`?

### F. Boundary
IDX-003 = after-commit pipeline + INDEXED/FAILED for that attempt.  
IDX-004 = retry/claim/max-attempts.  
No retrieval/chat/API.

**DO NOT IMPLEMENT. STOP FOR HUMAN REVIEW.**

PENDING → PROCESSING

============================================================
5. VERSION GATING — CRITICAL
============================================================

Event/request = `(ticketId, V)`.

Load the authoritative current MySQL SupportTicket.

Behavior:

A. current ticket version == V
   → continue pipeline

B. current ticket version > V
   → this event is stale
   → ABANDON this processing attempt
   → do not build/embed/write V
   → do not mark the newer request INDEXED or FAILED

C. current ticket version < V
   → invariant violation
   → attempt to mark FAILED only if requestedVersion is STILL V
   → use sanitized error information

The MySQL ticket @Version remains authoritative.

TicketChunkMetadata.ticketVersion must correspond to that same V.

============================================================
6. PIPELINE
============================================================

For a current request V:

1. Load authoritative SupportTicket.
2. Load ordered comments using existing repository/service behavior.
3. Build deterministic TicketKnowledgeDocument.
4. Map TicketDocumentMetadata.
5. Chunk using TicketDocumentChunker.
6. Embed using TicketChunkEmbeddingService.
7. Call TicketVectorIndexer.replaceTicketVectors(...).
8. Handle TicketVectorReplaceResult.

Do not modify DOC-001, DOC-002, EMB-001, EMB-002, or IDX-001/002 contracts
unless an actual compile/runtime blocker is discovered.

If such a blocker exists, STOP and report it before changing those contracts.

============================================================
7. PG RESULT
============================================================

If TicketVectorIndexer returns:

APPLIED:
    mark INDEXED only if the indexing-state row still has:
        requestedVersion == V

    Then:
        state = INDEXED
        indexedVersion = V
        clear lastError as appropriate

REJECTED_STALE:
    expected stale-work abandonment
    NOT a failure
    do NOT mark FAILED

    Do not let the old request overwrite the state of a newer request.

IDX-002 remains responsible for the PG-side stale-version fence.

============================================================
8. TERMINAL STATE UPDATES — CRITICAL
============================================================

ALL terminal state updates MUST be version guarded.

This applies to BOTH INDEXED and FAILED.

Never do:

old V fails
→ meanwhile V+1 is PENDING
→ old V marks row FAILED

That is forbidden.

For any failure while processing V:

mark FAILED only when:

    current indexingState.requestedVersion == V

If requestedVersion has advanced beyond V:
    abandon the old failure
    leave the newer request's state untouched.

Similarly:

mark INDEXED only when:
    requestedVersion == V

Use short independent MySQL transactions for state updates as appropriate.

PG/Ollama/DOC failures must NEVER roll back or alter the already committed
SupportTicket business change.

============================================================
9. FAILURE BEHAVIOR
============================================================

Handle these cases:

Ticket load failure:
    FAILED only if requestedVersion still V.

DOC/chunk failure:
    FAILED only if requestedVersion still V.

Embedding/Ollama failure:
    FAILED only if requestedVersion still V.
    No PG replacement should occur if embedding fails.

PGVector failure:
    FAILED only if requestedVersion still V.
    Ticket business data remains committed.
    IDX-001 transaction rollback preserves prior complete vectors.

IDX-002 inconsistent-version/fence exception:
    FAILED only if requestedVersion still V.

REJECTED_STALE:
    abandon; NOT FAILED.

Ticket advances to newer MySQL version while old V processes:
    old V must never mark newer request INDEXED or FAILED.

Sanitize persisted error text.
Do not persist stack traces, secrets, credentials, connection strings, or
sensitive infrastructure details in lastError.

Do NOT implement a new soft-delete/vector-deletion workflow in IDX-003.

The project currently has no product soft-delete mutation trigger requiring

Soft-delete vector cleanup remains deferred until its real trigger/path exists.

============================================================
11. MYSQL / PG TRANSACTION ISOLATION
============================================================

MySQL remains the transactional system of record.

Do not combine MySQL and PostgreSQL into one distributed transaction.

Business write:
    MySQL transaction commits first.

Processor state changes:

Vector replacement:

Downstream failure must never undo the committed ticket change.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
TicketChunkEmbeddingService requires an EmbeddingModel bean to start.

The real processor uses @ConditionalOnBean requiring both TicketVectorIndexer and TicketChunkEmbeddingService.

NoOp processor activates via @ConditionalOnMissingBean when SupportTicketIndexingProcessor is absent. TicketDocumentChunker is not a bean; it is constructed directly from properties. Assignee lazy loading requires a transactional load method. The implementation will add IndexingErrorSanitizer, TicketIndexingStateUpdater, and RAG support ticket indexing processor. State updates will use @Transactional with REQUIRES_NEW propagation.

markProcessing validates the requested version against the stored state before updating status to PROCESSING and resetting last error. Attempt counts increment on each processing attempt. Indexed and failed transitions reuse the same version guard.

The processor entry point attempts to mark the ticket as processing under the requested version. If the version changed during the check, it returns early. Otherwise it loads the ticket inside a fresh transaction. It verifies the version matches again. If the version advanced or the ticket disappeared, it marks the state failed and exits. Otherwise it proceeds through the full pipeline: fetch comments, build the document, chunk it, embed all chunks, and replace the vectors.

After the pipeline finishes, the processor marks the state indexed if the result is APPLIED and the version is unchanged. It returns immediately if the result is REJECTED_STALE. Any exception triggers a failed state update only while the version is still valid, with the error message sanitized. The claim logic allows a PENDING ticket with the matching version to move to PROCESSING, but blocks concurrent claims. A FAILED status firing unexpectedly is considered an unusual edge case.

The processor only transitions a ticket from PENDING to PROCESSING. It rejects claims for tickets already INDEXED or FAILED, even if the version matches.

A separate service will handle state transitions to avoid self-invocation problems with @Transactional methods. The ticket assignee will be loaded with Hibernate.initialize inside a transaction. The real processor requires both TicketVectorIndexer and EmbeddingModel beans, so the application may fail to start without Ollama or database credentials.

The NoOp processor activates when TicketVectorIndexer is absent, covering MySQL-only deployments. It also activates if an EmbeddingModel bean exists but the vector indexer does not, ensuring the fallback path remains correct regardless of which dependency is missing.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Writing the integration test SupportTicketIndexingProcessorIT.

The integration test uses MySQL and PostgreSQL Testcontainers. It relies on a fixed EmbeddingModel and the real RagSupportTicketIndexingProcessor. It covers the happy path, embedding failure, version advancement, and REJECTED_STALE. After-commit and rollback evidence reuse the lighter SVC-002 MySQL IT pattern.

A failing embedding service will be injected via @Primary to simulate embedding failure. The test structure includes happy path creation, update re-indexing, and version abandonment. Abandoned versions must not incorrectly mark the next version as FAILED or INDEXED.

The REJECTED_STALE test will use a simpler approach. It will create and index a ticket, then manually apply newer version embeddings through the TicketVectorIndexer.

A bug was discovered in the REJECTED_STALE handling. The current code leaves the ticket status as PROCESSING instead of reverting to PENDING. The approved plan specifies that REJECTED_STALE must abandon the version without marking it FAILED. The test will verify that abandoned versions return to PENDING rather than remaining stuck in PROCESSING.

The stuck PROCESSING bug is confirmed. When tryMarkProcessing succeeds, the ticket enters PROCESSING before the MySQL version check runs. If the version check later rejects the event, the ticket remains stuck in PROCESSING. The fix must restore PENDING whenever the requestedVersion matches the abandoned version.

A concurrent write may update the ticket to version V+1 and status PENDING before the abandonment check runs. The fix must leave that row untouched because the requestedVersion already matches the abandoned version.

The REJECTED_STALE fix will revert the ticket to PENDING whenever the requestedVersion still matches the abandoned version. This prevents the PROCESSING state from getting stuck when PostgreSQL holds a newer version. It also allows IDX-004 to retry the abandoned version later.

The `tryRevertToPending` helper is now defined with `@Transactional(REQUIRES_NEW)`. It reverts the ticket to PENDING only when the requestedVersion still matches the abandoned version and the status is PROCESSING. It skips reversion if the requestedVersion has already advanced, preventing concurrent updates from being overwritten.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A REJECTED_STALE test issue was identified. Processing a ticket at version v fails when MySQL still holds v while PostgreSQL already advanced to v+1.

The REJECTED_STALE path succeeds. But mutating the loaded ticket entity to version v+1 risks dirtying the Hibernate session. Since getActiveById is @Transactional, the entity detaches after the method returns.

Mutating the detached ticket entity for embedding metadata is safe because the ticket is never saved back to MySQL. Unused imports such as `assertThatThrownBy` should be removed. Ollama embedding dimensions must align with pgvector dimensions; both are set to 768 in `application.properties`. Unit tests will run first.

## A. Exact IDX-004 contract (`spec/tasks.md`)

| Field | Spec |

| **Verify** | Fail-then-success, max-attempt, concurrent claim, newest-version |
| **Complete when** | Failed current work can be retried safely using only persisted state |

Also: tasks.md summary — *“Explicit in-process retry only; no scheduler/broker/admin API.”*  
`rag-ingestion.md` §6: PROCESSING = claimed current requested version; retry reconstructs from MySQL (no stale payloads).

---

## B. Existing code/infrastructure to reuse

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `SupportTicketIndexingProcessor` / `RagSupportTicketIndexingProcessor` | Full DOC→EMB→IDX pipeline (call, don’t duplicate) |
| `TicketIndexingStateTransitionService` | Extend claim / terminal guards |
| `TicketIndexingState` + `@Version` | Optimistic concurrency for claim |
| `attemptCount`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastError` | Already on entity; IDX-003 increments on PROCESSING |
| `bootcamp.support-ticket.rag.indexing.max-retry-attempts` (= **3**) | `SupportTicketRagProperties.Indexing` — **only** retry knob today |
| `IndexingErrorSanitizer` | Sanitize failures |
| IDX-002 fence + IDX-003 version guards | Still protect PG / INDEXED |

**Do not reuse for IDX-004:** Quartz / `@Scheduled` (explicitly forbidden by task intent). Existing `SchedulerService` is unrelated Bootcamp cron.

---

## C. Proposed retry/claim flow

```
Explicit in-process entry (e.g. SupportTicketIndexingRetryService.retryEligible()
  or retryTicket(ticketId))
  → find eligible rows: status ∈ {PENDING, FAILED}
       AND attemptCount < maxRetryAttempts
       AND (optional) status≠INDEXED
  → for each (or one): CLAIM in REQUIRES_NEW MySQL tx
       PENDING|FAILED → PROCESSING
       only if status still eligible + attemptCount < max
       + bump attemptCount / lastAttemptAt (same as IDX-003 claim)
       + clear lastError
       [JPA @Version: loser gets OptimisticLockException → skip]
  → invoke SupportTicketIndexingProcessor.process(ticketId, claimedRequestedVersion)
  → existing IDX-003 outcomes: INDEXED / FAILED / abandon / revert
```

**Eligibility:** PENDING (missed/stuck after-commit) and FAILED (retryable).  
**Not eligible:** INDEXED; `attemptCount >= maxRetryAttempts`; (open) stuck PROCESSING.

**Invocation:** **explicit service method only** — no polling scheduler, no admin API, no broker.

---

## D. State-transition table

| From | Event | To | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| PENDING/FAILED | claim (eligible) | PROCESSING | attemptCount++ |
| PENDING/FAILED | claim but attemptCount ≥ max | unchanged → treat as terminal FAILED | no process |
| PROCESSING | IDX-003 success + version match | INDEXED | existing |
| PROCESSING | IDX-003 infra fail + version match | FAILED | existing |
| PROCESSING | stale / REJECTED_STALE | PENDING (revert) or untouched | existing IDX-003 |
| FAILED | searchable write (SVC-002) | PENDING, attemptCount=0 | existing reset |
| * | newer `requestedVersion` while old retry runs | old cannot INDEXED/FAILED newer | existing guards |

---

## E. Concurrency / version handling

- **Two claimers:** same row → one wins `save` via entity `@Version`; other skips.
- **Claim state:** PROCESSING (matches `rag-ingestion.md`).
- **Newer version mid-retry:** IDX-003 already refuses INDEXED/FAILED if `requestedVersion` moved; claim must snapshot `requestedVersion` at claim time and pass that `V` to `process`.
- **PG:** IDX-002 advisory lock + fence unchanged.
- **Worker crash in PROCESSING:** not covered by “claim PENDING/FAILED” alone — **open decision** (reclaim stale PROCESSING vs leave).

---

## F. Retry / max-attempt policy

| Item | Source / proposal |
|---|---|
| **Max attempts** | `SupportTicketRagProperties.getIndexing().getMaxRetryAttempts()` (default **3**, property already set) |
| **Backoff delay** | **None configured** — do not invent; explicit caller controls timing |
| **Retryable** | PENDING, FAILED with `attemptCount < max` |
| **Terminal** | `attemptCount >= max` → remain/mark FAILED; no further claim; sanitized lastError e.g. max attempts exceeded |
| **attemptCount** | Increment on successful claim (already IDX-003); reset to 0 on new searchable change (SVC-002) |
| **lastAttemptAt** | Set on claim |
| **lastError** | Clear on claim; set on FAILED via sanitizer |

---

## G. Minimum production changes

1. Extend `TicketIndexingStateRepository` (+ service): query eligible PENDING/FAILED by attempt bound.  
2. Extend `TicketIndexingStateTransitionService`: `tryClaimForRetry(ticketId)` allowing PENDING|FAILED → PROCESSING with max check (or shared claim used by IDX-003 + retry).  
3. New thin `SupportTicketIndexingRetryService`: claim → `processor.process(...)`.  
4. Wire `maxRetryAttempts` into claim (no new config keys unless human wants backoff later).

Prefer **one** shared claim method so AFTER_COMMIT and retry don’t diverge.

---

## H. Minimum tests

**Unit (primary):**  
- claim wins / optimistic-lock loser skips  
- FAILED → claim → process → INDEXED (fail-then-success via mocks)  
- `attemptCount >= max` → no claim / no process

- retry calls existing processor once (no pipeline duplication)

**IT (only if needed):** one Testcontainers MySQL case for concurrent claim on same row **or** real fail→retry→INDEXED; reuse fixed EmbeddingModel pattern only if unit can’t prove claim race. Prefer unit + optional single IT.

---

## I. Mismatches / blockers / open decisions

1. **No backoff property** — OK for explicit retry; confirm no delay required.  
2. **Stuck PROCESSING** after crash — reclaim policy undecided.  
3. **IDX-003 `tryMarkProcessing` is PENDING-only** — must extend for FAILED claims (or separate retry claim).  
4. **Who calls retry?** Spec forbids admin API/scheduler — plan = **in-process service method** (tests / future ops hook), not HTTP.  
5. AFTER_COMMIT already processes PENDING once; retry mainly recovers **FAILED** and rare missed PENDING.

**IDX-004:** claim + max attempts + invoke existing processor.  
**Out:** retrieval, ask API, generation, citations, UI, eval, E2E, DOC/EMB/IDX fence redesign, Quartz/admin retry API.
